hero.title: Prove you can
hero.text: Define and schedule every backup in the network — the directory, the issuing CA, Group Policy, DHCP, the repository and analysis configuration, the VLAN 40 business services, the log archive, and the living records — carry copies to the offline cabinet, and rehearse one real restore of SBD-DC02 in isolation. Follow the build, explore the dependencies, and keep the evidence.

sample: E: on each Windows server in the set; /srv/backup on each Linux server (sample)

scene.label: Interactive 3D lesson network showing the domain controllers, issuing CA, file and database servers, audit repository, the Tier 0 and Tier 1 administration seats, and the offline root CA that this course backs up, rehearses, and records.
scene.completeCaption: Every item in the recovery set has a verified backup, an offline copy under custody, and a rehearsed restore behind it. The recovery record has an owner and a next rehearsal date, and the evidence is ready for course 2.1.

nodes.name: SBD-DC01
nodes.title: SBD-DC01 · 10.0.10.10
nodes.description: The directory leads the recovery order. Its scheduled system state and critical-volume backup goes to its own protected volume, and the production Recycle Bin restore in lesson 5 runs against it.

nodes.name: SBD-DC02
nodes.title: SBD-DC02 · 10.0.10.11
nodes.description: Keeps its own independent backup, because replication is availability, not recovery. A copy of its virtual machine is the one restored in DSRM on the isolated recovery segment in lesson 5.

nodes.name: SBD-SUBCA01
nodes.title: SBD-SUBCA01 · 10.0.30.20
nodes.description: Schedules its own system state and critical-volume backup, and backs up its database, private key, and configuration with certutil and reg export to its protected backup volume. Only the backup’s hashes and custody record go into evidence, and a Tier 0 custodian carries the copy offline.

nodes.name: SBD-AUDIT01
nodes.title: SBD-AUDIT01 · 10.0.50.40
nodes.description: Its hashed log archives are already the protected record. This course adds the archive catalog to the recovery set, and the audit custodian carries a copy to the offline cabinet.

nodes.name: SBD-FS01
nodes.title: SBD-FS01 · 10.0.40.10
nodes.description: Backs up D:\Shares to its protected volume every night, with each file’s NTFS permissions, and keeps an ACL record and share-definition export so access can be checked or reapplied without restoring data.

nodes.name: SBD-SQL01
nodes.title: SBD-SQL01 · 10.0.40.20
nodes.description: A nightly SQL Server Agent job backs up the application databases with master, model and msdb, verified with RESTORE VERIFYONLY. master carries the logins the databases depend on, and the restore note puts it first.

nodes.name: AdminJumpBox01
nodes.title: AdminJumpBox01 · 10.0.60.10
nodes.description: The Tier 0 seat (rule A01). The controllers’ and CA’s backup schedules, the CA backup session, the Group Policy backup task, the Recycle Bin, the Tier 0 closing scans, and the production object restore all run from here.

nodes.name: SBD-ADMIN-SRV01
nodes.title: SBD-ADMIN-SRV01 · 10.0.60.20
nodes.description: The Tier 1 seat. The member-server schedules — SBD-DHCP01, SBD-MGMT01, SBD-REPO01, SBD-SPLUNK01, and the VLAN 40 servers — are set and hashed from here, the audit custodian’s separate sessions reach SBD-AUDIT01, and the member servers’ closing SCAP scans run here.

nodes.name: SBD-ROOTCA01
nodes.title: SBD-ROOTCA01 · Offline, no network address
nodes.description: Stays offline in the vault. Its protected backup from the course 1.1 ceremony is verified and its custody confirmed, never duplicated or copied onto the network.

flows.label: Tier 0 session · backup, GPO task, Recycle Bin, closing scan
Tier 0 session · backup schedule, closing scan
Tier 0 session · CA backup schedule, closing scan
Custodian and Tier 1 sessions · archive catalog, closing scan
Tier 1 session · share backup schedule, closing scan
Tier 1 session · database backup job, closing scan

stepTitles: Order the recovery set by dependency
Set recovery point and time objectives
Write the backup schedule in one place
Decide backup placement and access
Confirm the DSRM and root CA custody records
requirements.mistake: Writing objectives nobody intends to measure, such as a recovery time of minutes for a directory that has never been restored. Lesson 5 times a real restore against these numbers, so an aspirational value only guarantees a missed objective.
requirements.network: Everything in the recovery set already runs: both controllers on VLAN 10, the issuing CA on VLAN 30, the audit repository on VLAN 50, the member servers on their own VLANs, the business services on VLAN 40, with SBD-ROOTCA01 offline in the vault. No flows are shown: this lesson writes decisions, and no backup will ever cross the network to reach the offline cabinet.

control.name: Contingency Plan
control.body: A contingency plan names what must be recovered, in what priority, against which recovery objectives, and who is responsible. The ordered recovery set, its point and time objectives, and the placement and access decisions are the core of that plan for this network.
control.question: If the directory survived but the issuing CA did not, which items in your recovery set could you still trust, and which would wait?

checklist: I listed the recovery set in dependency order, directory first and VLAN 40 included, gave each item a measurable recovery point and time objective, and wrote the backup schedule that defines every backup.
I wrote who can write and read each protected backup volume, and recorded that no network path reaches the offline cabinet.
I confirmed the sealed DSRM passwords and the root CA’s ceremony backup are findable, without recording either secret.

stepTitles: Schedule system state backups on both controllers
Verify, record, and hash each backup
Back up the issuing CA under custody
Schedule the GPO backup with its links
Enable the Active Directory Recycle Bin
Write the restore decision tree
directory.mistake: Leaving out the critical volumes (wbadmin’s -allCritical) produces a backup that can restore system state on the same server but cannot rebuild a controller whose hardware is gone. Check that each scheduled job includes them before you record it as the full server recovery source.
directory.network: SBD-DC01, SBD-DC02 and SBD-SUBCA01 now each write a scheduled backup to their own protected volume, and SBD-DC01’s task backs up every GPO, so no backup traffic crosses the network. The flows are the Tier 0 sessions from AdminJumpBox01 on VLAN 60 that set the schedules, take the CA backup, and enable the Recycle Bin.

control.name: System Backup
control.body: System backup means copies at a defined frequency, with the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of the backup information protected. Two independent schedules on protected volumes, each verified and hashed, are that backup for the directory, the issuing CA keeps a password-protected backup under custody, every GPO is saved daily with its links, the Recycle Bin adds object-level recovery that never needs system state.
control.question: A deletion replicated to both controllers an hour ago. Which branch of your decision tree applies, and what would each other branch cost you?

checklist: I scheduled system state and critical-volume backups on SBD-DC01, SBD-DC02 and SBD-SUBCA01, each to its own protected volume, verified the first runs and hashed the catalog.
I backed up SBD-SUBCA01’s database, key, and configuration to its protected volume and recorded custody, with only the hashes in evidence.
I scheduled the GPO backup with its link export, enabled the Recycle Bin as a recorded change, and wrote the restore decision tree.

stepTitles: Schedule SBD-DHCP01 and the inventory
Back up SBD-FS01’s shares with their permissions
Back up SBD-SQL01’s databases and logins
Back up APPS01, WEB01, the repository and Splunk
Account for the log archive and its catalog
Export the boundary and living records
trust-state.mistake: Backing up SBD-SQL01’s application databases but not master. The logins live in master, so a rebuilt instance restores data whose users map to nothing; back up master, model and msdb with them, record the logins, and restore the instance’s logins first.
trust-state.network: Each member server writes its scheduled backup to its own protected volume or /srv/backup, set and hashed over Tier 1 sessions from SBD-ADMIN-SRV01 — the business services on VLAN 40 among them. SBD-AUDIT01’s archive and catalog join the set through the custodian’s sessions, and no backup crosses the network.

control.name: Protection of Information at Rest
control.body: Backups carry what they protect: share contents with their permissions, databases with their logins, and the private keys in SBD-WEB01’s and SBD-SPLUNK01’s archives. Volumes written only by the backup jobs, root-only /srv/backup directories, and evidence that holds hashes instead of contents protect that information at rest.
control.question: Which of this lesson’s backups would hand someone a working key or a copy of business data, and who can read each one today?

checklist: I scheduled SBD-DHCP01 with its restore note, D:\Inventory, and the repository and Splunk archives, and recorded each first run’s hashes.
I scheduled SBD-FS01 with its ACL record and share export, SBD-SQL01’s database job with the login record and restore order, and SBD-APPS01’s and SBD-WEB01’s backups with their certificates.
I added the log archive and catalog, router export, register, and exception record to the hashed catalog.

stepTitles: Assign custodians by tier
Hash, copy, and verify each backup on media
Record each handoff in the custody register
Retrieve and verify one copy as a test
offline-copies.mistake: Checking the hash on the protected volume but not on the media. A copy that was never verified after copying can be incomplete or unreadable, and you find out during lesson 5 or on the bad day; verify the hash on the media before it leaves the room.
offline-copies.network: No network flows are shown: the offline backup cabinet has no network path, so copies reach it only by hand. Tier 0 custodians carry the controller, CA, and policy backups, the audit custodian carries SBD-AUDIT01’s archive and catalog, and a Tier 1 custodian carries the member-server sets, the VLAN 40 servers’ included.

control.name: Media Storage
control.body: Media storage means physically controlling and securely storing media until it is sanitized or destroyed. The offline cabinet, encrypted media, matching hash pairs, and a register naming who stored what, when, and in which slot put that control into practice.
control.question: If a custodian left tomorrow, could someone else find, verify, and return every copy using the custody register alone?

checklist: I assigned custodians by tier, so no one carries a backup from a tier they do not hold.
I recorded matching hashes on the volume and on the media for every copy, and logged each handoff in the custody register.
I retrieved one copy using only the register, verified its hash, and confirmed it is readable.

stepTitles: Isolate the recovery segment first
Restore SBD-DC02’s system state in DSRM
Return to normal boot, verify, check the clock, tear down
Restore a test object from the Recycle Bin
rehearse.mistake: Attaching the restored copy of SBD-DC02 to a network that can reach the production VLANs. A controller carrying old directory state can push the past into the live forest, so write the isolation rule and confirm it before the restore starts.
rehearse.network: The rehearsal runs on the isolated recovery segment, which has no path to the production VLANs and is not drawn here. Back in production, the flow from AdminJumpBox01 to SBD-DC01 shows the Tier 0 session that brings a deleted test object back from the Recycle Bin.

control.name: System Recovery and Reconstitution
control.body: Recovery and reconstitution means returning the system to a known state within a defined time after a disruption. A timed restore that reaches a verified, healthy directory, measured against the lesson 1 objective, shows the capability exists instead of assuming it.
control.question: What did the measured time include that your lesson 1 objective did not account for?

checklist: I confirmed the recovery segment had no path to production before restoring the copy of SBD-DC02 in DSRM.
I timed the restore from decision to directory services running and recorded the honest number against the objective.
I removed the DSRM boot setting, verified the directory and recorded its clock offset, tore the rehearsal down, and restored a test object from the Recycle Bin.

stepTitles: Assemble the recovery record with an owner
Take the closing SCAP snapshot from each seat
Reconcile the three living records
Write the Build path’s closing note
record.mistake: Filing the recovery record without a named owner or a next rehearsal date. One rehearsal proves only today’s backups; without a calendar, the record ages into a claim nobody has tested since the network changed.
record.network: The closing SCAP scans run from each tier’s own seat: AdminJumpBox01 reaches the controllers and the issuing CA, and SBD-ADMIN-SRV01 the member servers, SBD-AUDIT01 among them. Every system in the recovery set now has a verified backup, an offline copy, and a place in the recovery record.

control.name: Contingency Plan Testing
control.body: Contingency plan testing means testing at a defined frequency, reviewing the results, and taking corrective action. The measured times, lessons learned, named owner, and scheduled next rehearsal in the recovery record turn one test into a repeating practice.
control.question: Which change to the network should trigger a rehearsal before the scheduled date comes round?

checklist: I assembled the recovery record with the backup schedule, both rehearsal results, the decision tree, a named owner, and a next rehearsal date, and sealed both halves.
I filed current SCAP results for every system, scanned from each tier’s own seat, with their triage.
I reconciled the inventory, register, and exception record, and wrote the Build path’s closing note.
